page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-expanded compute instance provisioned on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supplying 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates instruction extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, FMA, and BMI2, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrated strong throughput, achieving a PassMark memory score of 2755.21, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested configurations. Raw memory bandwidth reached 553.05 GB/s on small cached 16 KB read blocks, 62.15 GB/s on uncached 256 MB reads, and 39.95 GB/s on 256 MB writes. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating attached persistent block storage and separate networking allocation.

Computational benchmarks indicate strong single-core performance alongside dependable multi-core execution. The stress-ng single-core test recorded 2928.59, ranking in the top 25 percent, while multi-core stress-ng reached 11730.12. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1660.0 and a multi-core score of 6622.0, with clang software compilation reaching 8076.0. In memory and application testing, Redis achieved 8.97 million SET operations per second, and static web serving reached 10.63 GB/s throughput. Machine learning inference runs capably on small 135M models, processing 607.92 prompt tokens per second, but degrades on 7B models down to 18.65 tokens per second.

Resource allocation on c2d-highmem-8 provides cost efficiency by pairing dedicated compute cores with substantial memory volume without forcing adoption of larger vCPU counts. This configuration matches in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, compilation suites, and data preprocessing tasks where memory capacity takes precedence over massive thread counts.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is an x86_64 compute-oriented instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 32 MB of L3 cache, standard AVX vector support, and cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI, while omitting AVX-512 extensions and bundled local storage. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU execution and top-quartile memory throughput, with a PassMark memory score of 2755.21 and small-block memory reads reaching 553.05 GB/s. Application testing demonstrated 8.97 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.63 GB/s in web serving throughput. Because it delivers an elevated memory capacity relative to core count, c2d-highmem-8 is technically balanced for in-memory databases, Redis caches, data transformation jobs, and backend application servers requiring generous per-thread memory headroom.
